scope: Five-checkpoint low-learning-rate DROID View LoRA sweep
summary: A five-epoch rank-16 sweep at 1e-5 completed, but all five checkpoints regress on the difficult heldout episode 21 relative to the current 3e-5 epoch-1 candidate, so the route is not expanded to three-episode generation.
evidence: Training completed 455/455 steps on physical A800 GPU 6 and preserved epoch-0 through epoch-4 checkpoints.
All five episode-21 generations use seed 20260811, 15 inference steps, and the same frozen v10 contract.
Full-frame SSIM rises only from 0.282072 to 0.309136 across the sweep; best subject-ROI SSIM is 0.263164.
The current high-learning-rate candidate scores 0.403208 full-frame and 0.342756 subject-ROI SSIM on the same episode.
No low-learning-rate checkpoint passes heldout acceptance, so no checkpoint was promoted or expanded to episodes 60/77.
lessons: Lower learning rate plus more epochs does not recover the cross-view mapping on the hardest heldout scene under this control representation.
Single-hard-case checkpoint screening avoids unnecessary full heldout generation when every candidate is clearly dominated.
limitations: Only episode 21 was generated for the sweep after fail-fast selection; this is sufficient for rejection, not for broader ranking.
next_actions: Retain the high-learning-rate epoch-1 candidate as the pre-v11 reference and focus compute on temporal data diversity.
